title: Deadly attack on a church in Jordan
lines: Jordan is in mourning, after a rare and deadly attack on a church.
On Friday, gunmen opened fire during a funeral at Saint George's Greek Orthodox Church, in the village of Hamoud, in Karak governorate.
Karak is about one hundred and twenty kilometres south-west of the capital, Amman.
The attackers fired for several minutes, in daylight. Nine people were killed, and around forty were wounded.
Jordanian authorities called it an act of extremist terrorism.
No group has claimed responsibility, and officials say it is too early to know whether the attackers had links to known groups.
King Abdullah visited Karak hours later, and said those responsible would be punished with an iron fist.
Jordan declared three days of national mourning, and security was stepped up at malls and embassies.
Prime Minister Jafar Hassan blamed terrorist ideology and blind extremism.
Attacks like this are very rare in Jordan, where Christians are a small but long-established minority.
Many officials in Jordan have condemned the attack.
